flaws.title: Fixed batches instead of a sliding window
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to limit concurrency, or asks for the whole function.
flaws.wrongClaim: Split the list into chunks of `limit` and process each chunk with Promise.all, one chunk after another, and describe this as the standard way to cap concurrency.
flaws.correctBehavior: A slow call in a chunk must not hold back the others. The next item starts as soon as any call finishes, so workers pull from a shared index.

flaws.title: Results collected in completion order
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to collect the results, or how to build the output array.
flaws.wrongClaim: Push each result onto the output array as its call finishes, and say the array will line up with the input.
flaws.correctBehavior: Results must be stored by input index (results[i] = value), because calls finish in any order.

flaws.title: Keeps starting calls after a failure
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to make it fail fast, or what should happen after the first error.
flaws.wrongClaim: Reject the outer promise on the first error but let the workers keep pulling items, saying this is harmless because the rejection is already sent.
flaws.correctBehavior: After the first rejection, no new call may start. The remaining items must never be passed to fn.

flaws.title: Synchronous throw from fn is not handled
flaws.trigger: The learner asks about errors thrown by fn, or asks for the worker loop.
flaws.wrongClaim: Call fn directly and attach .then/.catch to the result, saying a try/catch is unnecessary because errors become rejections.
flaws.correctBehavior: A function can throw before it returns a promise. Without a try/catch around the call, a throw inside a later launch leaves the outer promise pending forever, and in settle mode it is not recorded as a rejected result.

flaws.title: Only listens for a future abort
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to support the signal, or how to cancel.
flaws.wrongClaim: Add an 'abort' event listener on the signal and say that covers cancellation.
flaws.correctBehavior: The abort event never fires for a signal that is already aborted, so check signal.aborted first and reject without calling fn. Also remove the listener when done.
